newsitem.title: INDIA: Car bomb death toll rises to 16 in India's Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: Car bomb death toll rises to 16 in India's Kashmir.

text.p: The death toll from a car bomb explosion in a crowded bus station in the northern city of Jammu rose to 16 on Sunday and a senior official accused a Pakistani intelligence service of carrying out the attack.

"This dastardly act was sponsored by Pakistan's ISI (Inter-Services Intelligence) and its agents with the intention of dividing the people on communal lines," Farooq Abdullah, chief minister of Jammu and Kashmir, said in a statement.
"The ISI doesn't want normalisation of relations between India and Pakistan and is...trying to create trouble in a bid to divide communities to further its ends," he added.
Police said they had found a severed head and torso at the scene of Saturday's blast, bringing the death toll to 16.
Hospital doctor Rakesh Gaudutra told Reuters about 70 people injured in the blast had received treatment, of whom six were in critical condition. About 20 had been discharged.
A five-year-old boy with a bandaged thigh lay crying in pain. He was sharing a bed with his injured father.

The right-wing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party called for a general strike in Jammu on Monday in protest at the bombing. Jammu, winter capital of India's Moslem-majority state of Jammu and Kashmir, is populated mainly by Hindus.

"I was drinking tea and suddenly there was a big bang and I could see parts of human bodies hurtling through the air," said Bhushan Kumar Gupta, the owner of a petrol station next to the bus station. "It was like an earthquake."
Gupta, whose leg was cut by flying glass, said he had been ferrying casualties to hospital when he heard a second blast.
However, Abdullah said there had been only one bomb.
"There was only one blast, not two as previously reported," Abdullah told Reuters in New Delhi by telephone on Saturday night. "We strongly condemn this attack."
Abdullah said the bomb was planted in a Gypsy, an all-terrain vehicle, and destroyed a tourist bus next to it.
"There were a lot of vehicles moving around. We don't know if the Gypsy was moving at the time," he said.

The bomb went off as several senior Jammu and Kashmir officials were driving along a street on the other side of the bus station towards a nearby stadium to attend a concert. Police said none of the officials were hurt. The concert went ahead.
Angry townsfolk set a government car on fire and damaged several others after the bombing, which wrecked several buses and shops, shattering windows up to 600 metres (yards) away.

The blast occurred on the second day of crucial talks between Indian and Pakistani diplomats in New Delhi, 500 km (300 miles) to the south. India and Pakistan have fought two wars over Kashmir since independence from Britain in 1947.
The last round of India-Pakistan talks collapsed in January 1994 over Kashmir, which is claimed by both countries.
More than 20,000 people have been killed since Moslem separatists launched a revolt in 1990 in the two-thirds of Kashmir controlled by India. Pakistan holds the rest of the Himalayan region.
